history.what: Planning docs: ARCHITECTURE, GAME_DESIGN, DESIGN, ROADMAP (39 tasks), CLAUDE.md, playbook, progress log. Original plugins 3.3.0 and 4.2.0 added under reference/.

Owner rules added: no women or sexual content anywhere; text uses only learned letters; scene levels follow learning progress. Content filter (src/learn/content.ts) applied to word packs, sentences and lesson texts.

manual_steps.title: Import the repo into Vercel
manual_steps.details: Go to vercel.com, sign in, click Add New > Project, pick the GitHub repo shlomyeisenberg-lang/Otiyot, keep the detected Vite settings and click Deploy. Main becomes the live link.
manual_steps.browser_prompt: Open https://vercel.com/new in my browser. Steps: 1) If asked to sign in, stop and hand control back to me. 2) Under Import Git Repository choose the GitHub repo shlomyeisenberg-lang/Otiyot (if it is not listed, click Adjust GitHub App Permissions and stop for me to approve). 3) Click Import. 4) Leave Framework Preset as Vite and keep the settings from vercel.json. 5) Click Deploy and wait until it finishes. Stop and hand control back to me for sign-in, passwords, 2FA, CAPTCHAs, payment, creating an account and pasting secret keys; never type a secret yourself. When done, report the live URL and what you did.

T02.summary: The typing engine every scene and mode will use now exists as pure logic: keyboard layouts for Hebrew and English, a session that judges each key, and scoring with per-key, per-finger and habit hints.
changes: src/core/layouts.ts: Hebrew (Israeli) and English (QWERTY) layouts by KeyboardEvent.code with finger, hand, row, shift layer, final letters, niqqud helpers, key lookup by character and text normaliser

src/core/session.ts: TypingSession (judged TypedKey out, errors never block, backspace policy allowed/disabled/mustFix, hardcore flag, niqqud ignore/required, works whatever the OS keyboard language is)
src/core/metrics.ts: gross and net WPM, accuracy, consistency, WPM timeline, rolling WPM, per-key and per-finger stats, confusion pairs, wrong-finger / home-row-drift / slow-key hints
tests/unit/core-layouts.test.ts and tests/unit/core-session.test.ts: 46 new tests incl. recorded Hebrew and English sessions and mixed Hebrew/English lines
docs/ROADMAP.md: T02 ticked

decisions.decision: The session takes the time as an argument instead of reading a clock
decisions.why: Keeps core pure and makes recorded-session tests exact

decisions.decision: Kept the reference shift layer (( on Shift+9 for Hebrew) and the swapped < > ; added mirrored brackets and backslash
decisions.why: Port behaviour from 4.2.0; brackets were missing there

decisions.decision: Niqqud marks can be typed in any order and a letter typed while marks are owed counts as a missed mark
decisions.why: Errors must never block the player

decisions.decision: Net WPM = gross WPM minus mistakes per minute, as in the 4.2.0 engine
decisions.why: Keeps scores comparable with the old plugin

T02.notes: Timing-based hints use simple thresholds; T06 (adaptive engine) may tune them.

T03.summary: Saves now exist as pure logic: several local profiles, a versioned save with migrations, browser and Otzaria storage chosen at boot, autosave that keeps the last good copy, JSON export/import and a one-time import of old plugin progress.
changes: src/save/schema.ts: Save/Profile types from ARCHITECTURE section 4, defaults, tolerant normaliser that repairs bad fields
src/save/migrations.ts: CURRENT_VERSION 1, migration chain, v0 (unversioned) to v1, refuses saves from newer versions
src/save/store.ts: SaveStore with localStorage, Otzaria (storage.get/set with a local mirror) and memory adapters; detectStore picks at boot
src/save/manager.ts: SaveManager with load + recovery (primary, then last good copy, then fresh), debounced autosave, profile create/rename/delete/switch, export/import JSON
src/save/legacy.ts: one-time import of old plugin progress (hebtyper_data_v2) into a new profile
src/main.ts: creates the SaveManager at boot, loads it, flushes on pagehide
tests/unit/save-*.test.ts: 40 new tests (round-trip, migration, corrupt recovery, both adapters with a mocked Otzaria, profiles, export/import, legacy import)
docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, CHANGELOG.md updated

decisions.decision: Version 0 is the unversioned early shape and the current version is 1
decisions.why: There was no older released format; this proves the migration chain works and leaves a clear place for the next change

decisions.decision: Hand-written validation instead of adding a schema library
decisions.why: Keeps the bundle small and avoids a new dependency; the normaliser repairs fields instead of rejecting the whole save

decisions.decision: Every autosave first copies the previous good save to a backup key
decisions.why: A half-written main save can then always be recovered from the last good copy

decisions.decision: A broken or too-new save is kept under otiyot_save_unreadable and a too-new save is never overwritten
decisions.why: Nothing the player earned is lost by an update or a downgrade

decisions.decision: Importing a profile file adds profiles (new ids on clash) unless replace is asked for
decisions.why: Safer: importing can never wipe existing profiles by accident

decisions.decision: Deleting the last profile creates a fresh one
decisions.why: The game always has a player

decisions.decision: Added meta.legacyChecked and createdAt to the schema
decisions.why: Makes the old-plugin import happen once only

Legacy import maps statistics and completed lessons only; old lesson ids are kept as they are and will be matched to the new tracks in T04

decisions.decision: Weak keys, weak transitions and the difficulty level are inputs to the text generators, not computed here

decisions.decision: The 4.1 "keep unlocked after key-order migration" list and the frequent-word chunk drills were not ported

decisions.decision: Tiers are by word length; row coverage is answered by the allowed-key filter

T06.summary: The adaptive engine is now pure logic in src/learn/adaptive.ts: it learns per-key, per-finger and per-letter-pair skill, picks weak keys and transitions, schedules spaced reviews, keeps difficulty near the 92 to 96 percent accuracy band, and builds drills deterministically from a seed. decisions.decision: Weak-key share in drills is clamped to 15-50 percent
decisions.why: Keeps the drill feeling like natural typing while still over-sampling weak keys, as the done-when test requires

decisions.decision: The unlock gate only blocks on keys that have at least 3 attempts and score under 70

decisions.decision: Menu letters also work through the physical key, on both layouts
decisions.why: A Hebrew menu must still answer when the computer keyboard is set to English (and the other way round); otherwise the gold letters would seem broken to half the players.

decisions.decision: Added five display settings to the save (schema v3) now instead of waiting for T36
decisions.why: Theme, colorblind, high contrast, large text and dyslexia font are part of the token system and must be remembered per player; T36 can build on them.

decisions.decision: New player steps are name, then keyboard, then lesson track
decisions.why: The track cards show the real first keys of each track, which depend on the keyboard chosen.

decisions.decision: On a first visit the three steps fill in the player that every new save already has, instead of adding a second one
decisions.why: Otherwise every device would start with an unused player called Player.

decisions.decision: Screens are addressed by the part after # in the address (for example #/settings)
decisions.why: It works the same on the website and inside Otzaria, where the game is opened from a folder, and makes every screen testable.

decisions.decision: The Journey item is shown on the main menu but faded and marked Soon

decisions.decision: Fonts are declared by hand (woff2 only, Hebrew and Latin subsets, only the weights used)
decisions.why: The ready-made @fontsource stylesheets would also ship older woff files and unused subsets and roughly double the size of the Otzaria plugin. OpenDyslexic is the largest single file (115 KB).

decisions.decision: The styleguide is left out of the real build
decisions.why: DESIGN.md says it is for development only. To see it: pnpm dev, then open #/styleguide.

decisions.decision: Charts and the keyboard picture always run left to right, also in Hebrew
decisions.why: A physical keyboard does not mirror, and time on a chart reads left to right in both languages.

decisions.decision: The frontend-design skill named in the roadmap was not available in the unattended run
decisions.why: The design was worked out from DESIGN.md directly and checked by looking at screenshots at 1366x768 and 375px, in both languages and themes.

T08.summary: The game now has its 3D foundation: a renderer with four graphics presets that picks the right one for each computer, lighting, fog, shadows and screen effects, a camera rig, a kit of gold-ink effects, modest robed characters animated by code, scene loading behind an ink wipe, and a test range that shows all of it.
changes: src/engine/engine.ts + loop.ts: one renderer, resize handling, fixed 1/60 s logic steps, hit-stop, frame statistics, simulate() for tests, dispose() that reports anything left on the graphics card
src/engine/quality.ts: presets low, medium, high, ultra and the 2-second first-run benchmark that picks one from measured frame times; budgets 150 draw calls and 300k triangles on medium
src/engine/materials.ts: MaterialKit, the one place surfaces are made, with the grey-to-color restoration sweep (gold wavefront, up to 6 at once), height fog with sun glow, flat low-poly shading
src/engine/lighting.ts: Atmosphere (sky, one hero sun, fill light, fog) with blob shadows on low, one shadow map on medium, three cascaded shadow maps on high and ultra
src/engine/postfx.ts: bloom, screen-space god rays, SSAO on high and ultra, chromatic-aberration hit pulse, tone mapping, color grading, screen flash, vignette
src/engine/camera.ts: camera rig with third-person follow and collision, rail and cockpit modes, shake and push-in; modes glide into each other
src/engine/vfx.ts: pooled effects moved by the graphics card: gold sparks, ink splashes, ink trails, letters breaking into fragments, shockwaves, restoration sweep, flash, combined impact
src/engine/letters.ts: every Hebrew and Latin letter drawn once into one texture; many floating letters in a single draw call
src/engine/character.ts + characterAnim.ts: modest robed figures (hat, cap or head scarf, optional beard and quill) with idle, walk, run, write, hit, stagger, fall, cheer and smooth blending
src/engine/scene.ts + transition.ts + disposal.ts: the GameScene and SceneContext contract, SceneManager, ink-wipe loading transition, disposal tracking with a leak check after every scene
src/engine/perf.ts: performance overlay (frames per second, frame time, draw calls, triangles, GPU objects, preset); compact on phones

src/scenes/range + src/ui/screens/range.ts + src/ui/styles/engine.css: the test range at #/range with buttons and number keys for every effect, camera, animation and preset; typing the floating word restores color
src/save/schema.ts + migrations.ts: save version 4 adds settings.quality and meta.autoQuality, with a migration and test
locales/he.json + locales/en.json: all test range and overlay strings in Hebrew and English
tests/unit/engine-kit.test.ts (20 tests) and tests/e2e/range.spec.ts (full tour, budget check, zero leaked GPU objects after closing); playwright.config.ts lets the test browser draw 3D in software
package.json: added the libraries three and postprocessing (listed in ASSETS.md)
docs: ARCHITECTURE section 7b (engine kit) and save v4, DESIGN 3D art direction note, CHANGELOG, ASSETS, ROADMAP tick

src/learn/source.ts: learnedWordSource, words built only from the letters the player has already learned (real words when enough letters are known, short letter drills before that); the test range uses it; tests/unit/learned-words.test.ts checks both languages and both tracks
src/engine/character.ts: headwear is a cap, a brimmed hat or a turban; the head scarf was removed and the walking figure in the range is now a bearded man in a turban

decisions.decision: Use the postprocessing library for screen effects instead of writing every pass by hand
decisions.why: It merges effects into one or two full-screen passes, which is what keeps bloom, god rays and grading affordable on integrated graphics.

decisions.decision: All surfaces are made by one MaterialKit that shares one set of shader inputs
decisions.why: The color sweep, fog and theme then work on every object in every scene without scene authors thinking about it, and a sweep costs nothing per material.

decisions.decision: Effects are animated on the graphics card from ring buffers
decisions.why: Spawning an effect writes a few numbers; nothing is allocated while playing, which the performance rules require.

decisions.decision: The benchmark runs on medium and judges steadiness, not just average speed
decisions.why: A browser never draws faster than the screen, so high is only chosen when 95 percent of frames are on time.

decisions.decision: The draw-call budget is enforced on low and medium only
decisions.why: ARCHITECTURE sets the budget for medium; high and ultra spend extra draw calls on cascaded shadows by design (about 260 in the range).

decisions.decision: On the night-ink theme the forgotten-world grey is lifted to a moonlit level
decisions.why: The dark fade token is nearly black; when I looked at the range in the dark theme the whole ground was pure black. It is now dim but readable.

decisions.decision: The test range is reached by address (#/range) and is not in the menus
decisions.why: It is a tool for building scenes, not part of the game.

decisions.decision: Audio and HUD are silent stand-ins in SceneContext for now
decisions.why: They are built in T09 and T10; scenes written today will not need changing when they arrive.

decisions.decision: With reduce motion on, shake, push-in, flash, chromatic pulse and hit-stop are switched off completely
decisions.why: Those are exactly the effects that bother motion-sensitive players; color sweeps and particles stay.

decisions.decision: Applied the two new owner rules (merged into main while this task was being built) inside this task
decisions.why: They are binding for every task: the range had one figure in a head scarf that could be read as a woman, and its words came from the whole library instead of the learned letters.

decisions.decision: Before enough letters are learned to spell real words, the range shows short drills made of the learned letters
decisions.why: A new player knows only two keys; nothing unlearned may ever be asked, so drills are the only honest text.

manual_steps.title: Check the frame rate on a real computer
manual_steps.details: The cloud build machine has no graphics card, so real speed could not be measured there. On your own computer open the live link, add #/range to the end of the address, click Medium under Quality and read the first line of the small box in the corner: it should say about 60 and not be red. Needs the live link from the T01 step (Import the repo into Vercel).
manual_steps.browser_prompt: Open the live Otiyot website in my browser (the Vercel address of the project shlomyeisenberg-lang/Otiyot; if you do not know it, open https://vercel.com/dashboard, open the project named otiyot and use its production address; if asked to sign in, stop and hand control back to me). Steps: 1) Add #/range to the end of the address and press Enter. 2) If the welcome steps appear, type the name Test, press Enter, then click Next twice, then go to the #/range address again. 3) Wait about 5 seconds until the 3D scene appears. 4) In the Quality group click Medium. 5) Wait 5 seconds, then read the small box in the top corner: frames per second, frame time, draw calls, triangles. 6) Press the number keys 1 to 9 one at a time and read frames per second again. 7) Click High and read the numbers once more. Stop and hand control back to me for sign-in, passwords, 2FA, CAPTCHAs, payment and creating an account; never type a secret yourself. When done, report the numbers you read for Medium and High, whether any number was shown in red, and what computer and browser this is.

todo: Real frame rate on integrated graphics is not yet confirmed (see the manual step); the measured load on medium is about 95 draw calls and 25k triangles, well inside the budget.
There is no graphics quality picker in Settings yet; for now it can only be changed in the test range. T36 adds it.
Scenes get silent audio and an empty HUD until T09 (HUD) and T10 (audio) are built.
The engine code is about 740 KB (187 KB compressed) and is loaded only when a 3D screen opens; menus do not pay for it.
The test range has no Easy / Standard / Hard levels: it is a developer tool, not a playable scene. Levels arrive with the combat and difficulty kit (T11).
T08.notes: Built by the Fable runner (Fable 5.2, effort Xhigh) over three attempts: the first two built the engine and the test range, the third looked at it in Chromium in both themes, fixed the black night theme and the phone overlay, and added the tests and docs. To try: open the live link, add #/range to the address, type the floating word and press the number keys 1 to 9; the arrow keys change the camera.

T09.summary: Typing now feels alive: a paper strip shows the word letter by letter with the next word dimmed, a tilted 3D keyboard under the game lights the next key in its finger color (also right after a mistake), a combo meter grows and changes material, and every key lands in the 3D world with gold ink, while mistakes blink the world grey without ever blocking.
changes: src/game/typing.ts: TypingDriver turns a text source into words (each finished by its space), judges keys with the typing core, keeps letter states, lookahead, combo and best combo, combo tiers, WPM, accuracy and metrics, and gives the finger guide its next key (Backspace when a mistake must be fixed); lesson (once) and endless modes
src/game/hints.ts: HintCoach shows rare, kind tips after mistakes: wrong finger (names the finger) and hands drifting off the home row; at most one per 25 seconds

src/game/feedback.ts: TypingFeedback, the shared 3D feel: gold ink stroke, sparks and ink drops and a small combo-scaled knock per right key; stumble and desaturate flicker per wrong key; gold ring, shockwave and impact per word
src/engine/worldText.ts: WorldText shows the word in the world as carved stone, a parchment banner or a hologram, right to left for Hebrew, colored by letter state
src/engine/scene.ts: SceneContext.typing (TypingView) and GameScene.onWord; SceneManager.onWord; src/engine/postfx.ts: setSaturationScale for the error flicker

src/ui/hud.ts + src/ui/styles/hud.css: HUD with combo meter (ink, techelet, silver, gold, light), WPM and accuracy pills, paper strip with per-letter states and lookahead, lesson progress bar, tips and gold announcements; implements the scene HudPort

src/ui/keyboardGuide.ts: CSS-3D tilted keyboard in the active layout (other layout small in the corner), finger color coding, next key raised in techelet, Shift to hold, press animation, optional hands, caption naming key and finger
src/ui/play.ts: PlayController wires keyboard -> typing driver -> HUD, guide, hint coach -> SceneManager.onKey / onWord
Design tokens: --finger-pinky, --finger-ring, --finger-middle, --finger-index, --finger-thumb (light and dark, mirrored in palette.ts and DESIGN.md), --key-u and --key-tilt
Save v5: settings.keyboardGuide (keys, hands, off) with migration and test; Settings > Typing has a Keyboard guide choice
Test range: types the current lesson with an end card (Enter for the next) or endless learned words; pickers for text style and keyboard guide; world word moved higher
Locales: HUD, guide, finger names, tips, settings and range strings in Hebrew and English

Tests: tests/unit/game-typing.test.ts (driver, guide after errors, must-fix, lessons, hardcore, WPM, combo tiers, hint coach, RTL layout, learned letters only), v4->v5 migration test, token test now also checks engine.css and hud.css; e2e range test types whole lessons in English and Hebrew by following the guide
Fixed a female name in the range e2e test save (content rule)
Docs: ARCHITECTURE 7c Typing in play, DESIGN tokens and in-play components, CHANGELOG, ROADMAP tick

decisions.decision: The 3D keyboard is drawn with CSS 3D transforms over the canvas, not in WebGL
decisions.why: Crisp glyphs in both layouts, token colors and themes for free, no second WebGL context or extra draw calls, and it works in the plugin

decisions.decision: Each word is typed together with the space after it, and the space finishes the word
decisions.why: Touch typing includes the space bar; it also gives a clear moment for the word-done effect

decisions.decision: Mistakes follow the profile backspace setting (default: the cursor moves on, Backspace can fix; must-fix shows Backspace in the guide)
decisions.why: Keeps the typing core rules from T02; nothing ever blocks unless the player chose must-fix

decisions.decision: Tips only after a mistake, at most one per 25 s and the same tip once per 90 s
decisions.why: Owner asked for gentle hints; frequent tips would nag

decisions.decision: Combo tiers at 10, 25, 50 and 100 correct keys in a row
decisions.why: Reachable early for learners, still special at the top

decisions.decision: Five new finger color tokens
decisions.why: Finger coding needs distinct hues and DESIGN forbids colors outside the tokens

decisions.decision: The test range does not record lesson results
decisions.why: It is a developer tool; real lesson recording belongs to the scenes and the hub

todo: Sounds for keys, errors and words come with the audio engine (T10); scenes already call audio.play(key, error, space, restore)
T09.notes: Try it on the live site at #/range: type the word on the paper strip and press space after each word.

T10.summary: The game now has sound, all made in code: five music themes that build layer by layer with your streak and always change on the beat, key clicks that climb the music's own scale, a soft knock for mistakes, menu sounds, place sounds that can come from a point in the world, four volume sliders and a sound room to hear everything.
changes: src/audio/theory.ts: modes (freygish, minor, dorian, mi sheberach), scale degrees to notes, the pentatonic click ladder (two octaves up and back), seeded random numbers, volume curve

src/audio/themes.ts: five themes as data: title (D freygish, 60, clarinet, 6/8), hub (G minor, 80, oud, brushes, swung), meadow (A dorian, 112, flute, darbuka), cliffs (E mi sheberach, 92, violin, kanun, 6/8), boss (C freygish, 138, strings, cello ostinato, taiko, three phases with the last one a semitone higher)

src/audio/composer.ts: the composer writes every bar of five stems (drone, pulse, melody, counter-melody, percussion); melodies in 4-bar phrases following a contour, ending each section on the tonic, with ornaments that change on every visit so ten minutes never loop exactly; stemLevels and tierIntensity (which stems play at which combo tier); BarClock holds intensity, section and boss-phase changes until the next bar line

src/audio/synth.ts: instruments made from oscillators, filters and noise: pad, harp, oud, kanun, flute, clarinet, violin, strings, cello, bell; darbuka, frame drum, taiko and brush kits; a hall reverb made from decaying noise

src/audio/sfx.ts: one-shot sounds: key (wooden tap coloured per character plus a note on the ladder, brighter per tier), space, error (low muted knock), word, perfect, restore, tier chime, impact, impact-small, shatter, whoosh, success, and menu sounds ui-move, ui-click, ui-back, ui-open, ui-toggle, ui-error
src/audio/ambience.ts: looping place sounds wind, birds, water, fire, crickets, machine hum, each optionally at a point in the world

src/audio/engine.ts: AudioEngine: starts only after the first key press or click (browser rule), mixer with music, effects, voice and menu buses plus limiter, music ducking under errors and impacts, look-ahead scheduler, stems fading over one beat at bar lines, positional one-shots and ambience (HRTF), listener, pause while the tab is hidden, status snapshot, offline render for tests

src/engine/scene.ts: AudioPort grows playAt, section, ambience, clearAmbience and listen (SILENT_AUDIO updated); SceneManager points the ears along the camera every frame and stops ambience when a scene unloads

src/ui/shell.ts + src/ui/app.ts: one AudioEngine for the app (AppContext.audio), volumes applied from settings, menus play the title theme softly, menu sounds on clicks, keyboard moves and Back; Screen.ownsMusic

src/ui/screens/sound.ts + screens.css: the sound room at #/sound (from Settings > Sound): theme cards, streak-level slider, stem lamps, a typing pad that builds a real streak, boss phase buttons, stop, place sounds and every effect

src/ui/screens/settings.ts: Sound tab has four volume sliders (music, effects, voice, menu sounds) and a button to the sound room; the old "sound comes later" note removed; new sound icon in src/ui/icons.ts
Save v6: settings.voiceVolume (0.9) and settings.uiVolume (0.6) with migration v5 -> v6 and test
Test range: plays the meadow theme with wind and birds in the trees; music layers follow the combo tier, new tiers chime, key clicks carry the typed character, words ring
Locales: sound room, theme names and moods, modes, stems, tiers, places, effects and new settings strings in Hebrew and English

Tests: tests/unit/audio-music.test.ts (theory, click ladder, volume curve, every theme well formed and distinct, ten minutes of every theme and boss phase in tune, in time and in range, determinism, recognisable but not looping, cadences on the tonic, layering, bar-synced changes, boss phases); tests/e2e/sound.spec.ts (every theme renders clean sound without clipping and layers add to it, sound wakes only on a key, a typed streak brings in the drums on the bar and a mistake takes them out, boss phases, place sounds, four saved volumes)
Docs: ARCHITECTURE 7d Audio and the save model, DESIGN Sound direction (how it was built), CHANGELOG, ASSETS (no audio files), ROADMAP tick

decisions.decision: Music layers follow the combo tier directly: ink = drone and soft harp, techelet = melody, silver = drums, gold = second voice, light = busier drums and fills
decisions.why: The roadmap says stems build with the combo; using the same five tiers as the HUD combo meter makes what you see and what you hear match

decisions.decision: After a mistake the layers drop back on the next bar line, with a one-beat fade, not instantly
decisions.why: Errors must stay soft ("impact without punishment"); a bar-synced fade sounds musical instead of like a penalty

decisions.decision: Key clicks are tuned to the theme that is playing and climb its pentatonic ladder two octaves, then back down
decisions.why: A long streak then plays a melody in key with the music instead of rising out of hearing or clashing

decisions.decision: Menus play the title theme quietly (melody, no drums); 3D screens and the sound room choose their own music
decisions.why: Menus feel alive without being noisy; scenes stay in charge of their own sound

decisions.decision: Added voiceVolume (0.9) and uiVolume (0.6) to the save as a new version (v6) with a migration
decisions.why: The roadmap asks for music, effects, voice and UI volumes; menu sounds start a bit lower so they never tire

decisions.decision: Voice volume is exposed as a number for speech synthesis instead of routing speech through Web Audio
decisions.why: Browser speech cannot be routed through Web Audio; T35 will set the utterance volume from it

decisions.decision: The AudioPort that scenes use gained playAt, section, ambience, clearAmbience and listen; the scene manager moves the ears with the camera and stops ambience on unload
decisions.why: Positional sound and boss phases need these, and doing the listener and cleanup in the manager means no scene can forget them

decisions.decision: Added a sound room screen (#/sound, opened from Settings > Sound)
decisions.why: There are no game scenes with music yet besides the test range; the sound room lets the owner hear every theme, layer, place and effect right away

decisions.decision: Quality is checked by rendering every theme offline in the browser test (real samples: not silent, no clipping, louder with more layers) plus unit tests that compose ten minutes of every theme
decisions.why: An unattended run cannot listen; these checks prove the music is in tune, in time, varied and clean

decisions.decision: Brushes in the hub theme swish softly through a band-pass filter instead of a bright high-pass hiss
decisions.why: A spectrum check of the first version showed the hub was too hissy for a cosy room

todo: Listen to the five themes in the sound room and say what to change (tempo, instruments, mood): the music was checked by measurement, not by ear
Themes for the other regions (Forge, Shuk, Jaffa Line, Geniza, Hermon, Station, Atbash City, Midbar, Lantern Caves, Keeper) come with their scene tasks; the voice bus is used by spoken lines in T35
The richer instrument and mix pass is part of T34 (art, lighting, VFX and music pass)
T10.notes: No typing text is produced in this task (the sound room counts any letters only for sound), so the learned-letters test does not apply. No audio files: everything is synthesized live, so the plugin stays small and offline.
